newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P places Italy's BPV ratings on creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P places Italy's BPV ratings on creditwatch.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said it has placed its 'A' long-term and 'A-1' short-term counterparty ratings of Banca Popolare di Verona-Banco S. Geminiano e S. Prospero SCRL's (BPV) on creditwatch with negative implications.

S&P said in a statement that the rating action follows the announcement that BPV wil acquire 56.8 percent of unrated Lombardy-based Credito Bergamasco (Creberg) from Credit Lyonnais. Once BPV has secured Credit Lyonnais's majority stake it will have to launch a public bid for Creberg's remaining capital.
BPV is the fourth-largest cooperative bank in Italy with 28 trillion lire total consolidated assets at end-1996. Its core activity is business and retail banking.

"Creberg's acquisition fits well with BPV's strategy of expanding into areas neighbouring its home base in northeastern Italy. Creberg is approximately half the size of BPV and is similarly focused on retail and small businesses.
"However, the acquisition price, which values 100 percent of Creberg's shares at around 2.185 trillion lire includes a significant amount of goodwill," the S&P statement said.
"This CreditWatch resolution will depend on clarification regarding the financing of the acquisition and its impact on BPV's financial profile, in particular on its capitalisation."
